speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what will be the impact of the recent global shipping disruptions on local consumers and businesses; and (b) whether the Government will consider having more mitigating measures to counter such impact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: However, I welcome any supplementary questions the Member may have on this topic.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: Given that lower-income households spend large proportion of their income on food and much of Singapore's food is imported, to what extent does the Ministry anticipate these shipping uncertainties to impact the prices of essential food items that matter most to the lower-income families in the near and mid-term?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It is an important question and it is a good reminder that incidents very far away can have an impact on a small resource-constrained nation like ours.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Government agencies do have also many tools in the toolbox that we can use to act against any of these disruptions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, that is effectively stock-piling critical supplies, including food.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In line with this, Singapore's food import costs should continue to fall and exit downward pressure on food inflation over the course of the year.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And finally, fiscal policy, which I think we will discuss more in this year's Budget.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And that is to help with the cost of living, including lower-income households.
